> **Deliverable:** D5, agent session transcripts with annotated human
> interventions. This is the single consolidated document for the team. It
> contains one labelled part per student, and each part states the fidelity of
> its own record.
>
> **Submission tree:** `dev` (ADR-007). **Harness:** OpenCode v2.2.5 (Part A).
> **Model:** `deepseek-v4-flash`.
>
> **Companion files:** the seven per-session exports under
> `transcripts/60760270-CUIHaoyu-*.md` remain the raw per-session records of
> record; this document reproduces their text in Part A. No annotation was
> changed when consolidating: the interventions are reproduced as recorded.

## 0. How to read this document

| Part | Student | Student ID | Records | Lines | Fidelity |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| A | CUI Haoyu | 60760270 | 7 annotated sessions (01–07) | 25,531 | verbatim OpenCode session exports, annotated after the session |
| B | Fan Hao | 60835652 | 1 session record (10 topics) | 565 | **retrospective reconstruction**, not a verbatim transcript |
| C | ZhuXuan | 60377218 | 1 supervision summary (6 stages) | 24 | **summary and evidence index**, raw session export not available |

**Annotation legend (Part A).** `TASK` = stage goal; `APPROVE`, `REJECT`,
`REDIRECT`, `AUTHORIZE`, `RESOLVE`, `DEFER` = a student intervention, each with
its rationale. Annotations were added by the student reviewer after the session
and are not part of the agent output.

**Integrity statement.** The course requires complete, raw transcripts as the
primary evidence of authentic human authorship. This document does not pretend
that all three records are equally raw:

- **Part A is raw.** Each file is an OpenCode session export with tool calls
  and results, plus annotations inserted at the intervention points.
- **Part B is a reconstruction.** The file states this in its own header; it
  paraphrases the user prompts and condenses the assistant answers. It is
  evidence of the decisions taken, but it is not the raw export.
- **Part C is a summary.** The raw session is not in the repository; the
  summary records the intervention points and links the commits and reports
  that can be checked.

The gap for Parts B and C is carried in `docs/debt-register.md`; the team must
produce the raw exports for those two members before a final submission, or the
report must declare them as summaries.

#### Turn 1 — Student

> **[TASK — requirements classification stage]** The student opens the stage with a read-only mandate and a file:line citation requirement. Rationale: the classification must be auditable against the registry, and it must not mutate authoritative artifacts before the team has decided on the findings.

"You are the coding agent for our CS5351 team project. Read AGENTS.md first, then architecture-blueprint.md, then docs/req/requirements.yaml and docs/req/req-schema.json.

This session is the REQUIREMENTS CLASSIFICATION stage only. Do NOT modify any file, and do NOT write code.

Deliver all of the following in your response:
1. Classify each of the five requirements by its D1 type, and check whether its fit_criterion is genuinely machine-checkable. Flag any requirement whose type or fit criterion does not match the D1 definition.
2. Check type coverage against the required types: functional, invariant, quality, performance, cost, governance, security. Report which required types have no requirement and whether that is a defect for our project scope.
3. For the two requirements in our implementation scope, REQ-HARD-GUARDRAIL and REQ-TRACEABILITY, restate the observable behaviour and the exact acceptance conditions a deterministic offline test could check.
4. List any ambiguity, conflict, or missing source link you find in the existing registry.

Cite file paths and line numbers for every claim. Stop after the review and wait for my approval. Do not save the review to a file yet."

# Structural Constraints (D3)

> Module organization rules. Each architectural element maps to exactly one
> module; new work extends the existing baseline, never replaces it; every
> module and function references the architecture decision and invariant it
> implements.

## Module mapping (seed)
| Architectural element | Module (in `src/`) | ADR / requirement | Invariant |
|-----------------------|--------------------|-------------------|-----------|
| Context assembler | `src/context_assembler.py` | ADR-001 / REQ-CONTEXT-BUDGET | INV-CONTEXT-BUDGET |
| Structured debater | `src/structured_debater.py` | ADR-002 / REQ-STRUCTURED-DEBATE | — |
| Trace recorder | `src/trace_recorder.py` | ADR-003 / REQ-TRACEABILITY | INV-TRACE-COMPLETENESS |
| Guardrail | `src/guardrail.py` | ADR-004 / REQ-HARD-GUARDRAIL | INV-GUARDRAIL-ZERO-ESCAPE |
| Termination controller | `src/termination_controller.py` | ADR-005 / REQ-TERMINATION-DISCIPLINE | — |

## Rules
1. One architectural element ↔ exactly one module.
2. New work extends the baseline; never replaces an unchanged module without an ADR.
3. Every module and function references the architecture decision and invariant
   it implements (header docstring: `ADR-xxx`, `REQ-...`, `INV-...`).
4. Authority boundaries: architecture blueprint and covenant are authoritative.

### Requirements Classification Review (D1 gate)

##### 0. Sources of authority for this review

- Type vocabulary + conventions: `docs/req/requirements.yaml:5-10`, `:22-30`
- Machine rules: `docs/req/req-schema.json:57-69` (type enum), `:78-81` (fit criterion definition), `:82-86` (MoSCoW)
- Behavioural definition of "invariant": `docs/architecture/invariants.md:3-4`
- Test obligation: `AGENTS.md:75-84`, `docs/code-governance/verification-constraints.md:7-12`

> **Caveat up front:** the D1 lectule spec itself is **not in the repository**. The only D1 text available is the file's own header (`requirements.yaml:5-10`) and the schema's descriptions. Anything I say about "the D1 definition" is therefore grounded in those two artifacts plus `invariants.md:3`. If the slide deck says something different, that deck wins — see A0 below.

---

#### 1. Type classification and fit-criterion checkability

##### REQ-CONTEXT-BUDGET — `performance` — **type: MISMATCH**

- Declared: `requirements.yaml:37` `type: performance # resource/context efficiency`
- **Defect.** Token consumption is *resource consumption*, and the registry's own vocabulary assigns that to **`cost`** (`requirements.yaml:28`: "cost : resource consumption (token, wall-clock) budgets"), while `performance` is "latency / throughput / efficiency targets" (`:27`). This requirement is a pure token budget with no latency or throughput clause anywhere in its statement (`:39-44`). Its header comment even calls it "(cost / performance)" (`:34`), i.e. the author was undecided and resolved it the wrong way. `req-schema.json:68` delegates the definition to D1, so the schema cannot catch this.
- **Also**: `registry_notes.token_efficiency_requirements` lists it as token efficiency (`:219`), which confirms the intent is `cost`.
- **Fit criterion is only *partly* checkable.** Machine-checkable fragments:
  - `context_tokens_injected_per_call <= CONTEXT_BUDGET` (`:46-50`) — checkable, provided "tokens" has one definition (see A5).
  - Compaction triggers when raw context > 6000 (`:50-51`) — checkable.
  - **Not reliably checkable:** "critical invariants and standing constraints survive re-injection" (`:51-53`) — no metric, no threshold. And "faithfulness score drops by no more than 0.1" (`:53-54`) requires an external judge (DeepEval), which is a **live/API** test — it cannot live in `test/offline/` (`AGENTS.md:48,83-84`; `verification-constraints.md:21-23`). So a fit criterion that `AGENTS.md:77` requires to have "at least one test" is unmeetable in the offline suite unless the judge is stubbed.
- **Verdict:** flag `fit_criterion_machine_checkable: true` (`:67`) as **overstated**; should be partial.

##### REQ-STRUCTURED-DEBATE — `quality` — **type: questionable**

- Declared: `requirements.yaml:73` `type: quality # structure / discipline of agent debate`
- **Defect (soft).** "Each turn exposes four mandatory fields, schema-validated at 100%" (`:75-81`) is a description of *observable output shape* — that is the `functional` definition (`:24`: "observable behaviour of the application"). `quality` is defined as "quality attribute (e.g. usability, maintainability)" (`:26`), which is a property of the system rather than an output contract. The requirement is a hybrid: a *functional* schema contract plus a *quality*-shaped convergence clause. As written, the functional half is the dominant, testable half.
- **Fit criterion is half-checkable.**
  - Checkable: schema pass rate `== 100%` (`:83-87`).
  - **Not checkable:** "early termination works: when `|bull_position - bear_position| <= DIVERGENCE_THRESHOLD`, the debate stops" (`:87-90`) — **`bull_position` and `bear_position` are never defined as anything numeric**. The four-turn schema (`:78`) is `claim → evidence_reference → counter_argument → round_conclusion`, all prose. There is no scalar produced by the schema that could be subtracted. As specified, this clause is *unimplementable and untestable*. Also `DIVERGENCE_THRESHOLD` has no default value, unlike every other threshold in the file (compare `:47` 8000, `:50` 6000, `:98` 1, `:194` 3).
  - Also `src/structured_debater.py:3` declares only field *names* (`DEBATE_SCHEMA = [...]`), not a JSON schema with types/required — so "validated against the defined JSON schema" (`:85`) currently has no schema to validate against.
- **Verdict:** flag `fit_criterion_machine_checkable: true` (`:104`) as **overstated**.

##### REQ-TRACEABILITY — `functional` — **type: correct**

- Declared: `requirements.yaml:110` `type: functional`
- "Every critical assertion must be recorded as a traceable link assertion_id → snapshot_id → source + timestamp, and the final decision re-traceable" (`:112-117`) is observable application behaviour → matches `:24`.
- **Fit criterion is checkable**, with one gap: "critical" is never defined. `:117-118` says non-critical assertions are "recorded optionally", but nothing states *which* assertions are critical. `:122` asserts "per-critical-assertion field completeness == 100%" — `== 100%` of an **undefined set** is vacuously true or arbitrary. This is the single biggest specification hole for this requirement (see A4).
- **Verdict:** type correct; `fit_criterion_machine_checkable: true` (`:137`) acceptable **only after** "critical" is defined.

##### REQ-HARD-GUARDRAIL — `invariant` — **type: correct, but the schema cannot enforce what makes it an invariant**

- Declared: `requirements.yaml:143` `type: invariant # zero-tolerance safety boundary`
- Matches `invariants.md:3` ("non-negotiable rule with a zero-tolerance fit criterion") and the criterion is genuinely zero-tolerance: `THRESHOLD: == 0` (`:157`), explicitly offline (`:160-162`).
- It is registered as an invariant in the register too (`invariants.md:8`, `:11` — `INV-GUARDRAIL-ZERO-ESCAPE`, `INV-RATING-VALIDITY`).
- **Structural tension to flag:** the type is `invariant`, but the three limits it enforces are "configurable" and carry **defaults** (`:149-151`, `:166`). "Zero tolerance" applies to the limit *as configured*, not to the default values — the requirement does not say so explicitly. `risk-list.md:7` already records this assumption ("Guardrail limits (10% / cash) are safe for all asset types").
- **Fit criterion is checkable** (§3 below).
- **Verdict:** no defect in type fit. Note (c) = "sell short more than available cash" (`:150-151`) is expressed in `src/guardrail.py:4` as `max_short_pct_of_cash: 1.0`, so the unit is clear (100% of cash). Good.

##### REQ-TERMINATION-DISCIPLINE — `performance` — **type: MISMATCH**

- Declared: `requirements.yaml:181` `type: performance`; header says "(performance / reliability)" (`:178`).
- **Defect.** Nothing in `:183-189` mentions latency or throughput. It is a *functional* behaviour ("the loop must detect X and stop with a logged reason") with a reliability flavour. Per `:27` vs `:24`, this should be `functional` (or `quality` if framed as reliability/discipline). The one arguably performance-flavoured clause is "No hard cap exceeds the configurable max tool rounds" (`:196-197`), and that is really a *governance* constraint on configuration.
- **Fit criterion is mostly checkable.**
  - Checkable: `terminates == True` on synthetic stall/repeat (`:193-196`); logged trigger name on every forced termination (`:195-196`).
  - **Weak:** "stalled progress" (`:186`) has **no threshold, no metric, no default** — only `REPEAT_THRESHOLD` (`:194`) and budget exhaustion are operationalised. A test cannot assert termination on "stalled progress" as written.
  - **Ambiguous:** "every forced termination writes a logger record naming the **trigger**" — the set of legal trigger names is not enumerated, so a test cannot assert an exact string; and `:192` uses "logged reason" while `:195-196` says "names the trigger". Two different assertions.
- **Verdict:** flag `fit_criterion_machine_checkable: true` (`:211`) as **overstated** (partially checkable: repeat + budget are; stall is not).

##### Summary table

| Req | Line | Declared type | Correct type | Fit criterion checkable? | `..._machine_checkable` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| REQ-CONTEXT-BUDGET | `:36-37` | performance | **cost** | partial (quality clause needs live judge) | `true` @`:67` **overstated** |
| REQ-STRUCTURED-DEBATE | `:72-73` | quality | functional (+quality) | partial (positions undefined) | `true` @`:104` **overstated** |
| REQ-TRACEABILITY | `:109-110` | functional | functional ✔ | yes, after "critical" is defined | `true` @`:137` OK w/ caveat |
| REQ-HARD-GUARDRAIL | `:142-143` | invariant | invariant ✔ | yes | `true` @`:175` OK |
| REQ-TERMINATION-DISCIPLINE | `:180-181` | performance | **functional** | partial ("stall" undefined) | `true` @`:211` **overstated** |

**Two hard type mismatches** (`performance` used for token cost and for loop termination), **one soft mismatch** (`quality` for an output-shape contract). Four of five claims of `fit_criterion_machine_checkable: true` are overstated.

#### 2. Type coverage against the seven required types

Present: `functional` (`:110`), `invariant` (`:143`), `quality` (`:73`), `performance` (`:37`, `:181`). That is **4 of 7 families represented by label** — but if I apply the corrections in §1, the corrected distribution is `cost` 1, `functional` 2, `invariant` 1, `quality` 1, and **`performance` becomes empty**.

| Required type (`requirements.yaml:7`) | Count | Status |
|---|---|---|
| functional | 1 (`:110`) | present |
| invariant | 1 (`:143`) | present |
| quality | 1 (`:73`) | present (weakly) |
| performance | 2 (`:37`,`:181`) | **mislabeled** — zero genuine latency/throughput requirement |
| **cost** | 0 | **absent** |
| **governance** | 0 | **absent** |
| **security** | 0 | **absent** |

##### Is each absence a defect for *our* scope?

- **`cost` — absent → TRUE DEFECT, high severity.** The #1 architectural driver is literally "Token cost is high" (`architecture-blueprint.md:23-24`), and the registry's own `registry_notes` names a `token_efficiency_requirements` bucket (`requirements.yaml:219`). Yet the `cost` type is never used. The fix is a one-word relabel of `REQ-CONTEXT-BUDGET` (`:37`) to `cost`, but it is a *real* gap: nothing in the registry is classified as the project's primary driver.

- **`security` — absent → DEFECT of label, not of substance.** The safety boundary exists and is called out as "safety / access-control boundaries" territory: the section header reads "deterministic safety boundary (invariant / **security**)" (`requirements.yaml:140`), and the blueprint calls it "require a deterministic safety boundary (zero tolerance)" (`architecture-blueprint.md:28-29`) inside a section on authority and permissions (`:54-63`). But `REQ-HARD-GUARDRAIL` is tagged **only** `invariant` (`:143`). The schema's `type` is a single string (`req-schema.json:57-68`) and there is no `types` array, so one requirement cannot carry both. Consequence: a grader scanning for a `security`-typed requirement finds none, even though the team clearly intended one. This needs a decision — either retag `REQ-HARD-GUARDRAIL` as `security` (losing its invariant status in the enum) or add a second, thin `security` requirement (e.g. "no API key appears in any logged artifact", which is already half-specified at `memory-design.md:25`). **This is a genuine open decision, not a doc typo.**

- **`governance` — absent → DEFECT, medium severity.** The project is saturated with governance rules that have *no* corresponding requirement: the no-non-agentic-modification rule (`Prompt.md:52-53`, `.opencode/rules.md:11`), the mandatory AI-use-log update (`Prompt.md:55-56`, `.opencode/rules.md:12`, CI gate at `.github/workflows/ci.yml:64-77`), the human-gate-before-code rule (`Prompt.md:29-32`, `.opencode/rules.md:8-9`), and the ADR-required-for-safety-critical rule (`.agent/rules.md:17-19`). These are enforced by CI and by covenant, so the *behaviour* exists — but `AGENTS.md:77` and `verification-constraints.md:7` bind tests to **fit criteria in the registry**, so a governance behaviour with no registry entry has no test obligation. Note also `docs/ai-use-log.yaml:8` currently has `entries: []`, so the governance gate is enforcing against an empty log — worth a `governance` requirement tying the gate to a testable predicate.

- **`performance` — zero genuine → DEFECT, low severity, *provided one is added or the label restored*.** The blueprint's verification section offers only quality thresholds and guardrail escapes (`architecture-blueprint.md:89-90`); there is no latency clause anywhere. So a genuine `performance` requirement does not exist and is arguably not needed — but then the "required types" claim in `requirements.yaml:7` is unmet. This is a scope statement problem more than an engineering gap.

**Overall:** 3 of 7 required types have zero requirements. For this project's stated scope, `cost` and `security` are **substantive defects** (both are top-2 architectural drivers per `architecture-blueprint.md:23-29`). `governance` is a **real but lighter defect** because the governed behaviour exists in CI/covenant without a registry anchor. `performance` is a **labelling defect**, resolved either by adding a latency requirement or by amending the intro claim at `requirements.yaml:7` — and amending that file needs an ADR + trace update per `AGENTS.md:52`.

#### 3. The two in-scope requirements: observable behaviour + exact deterministic acceptance conditions

##### 3a. REQ-HARD-GUARDRAIL — statements at `requirements.yaml:142-175`, ADR at `adr/004-hard-guardrail.md:12-15`, invariants at `invariants.md:8,11`, fallback at `runtime-policy-catalog.md:7`

**Observable behaviour** (the only externally visible contract): *a decision object is either passed through unchanged, or is replaced by the REVIEW/HOLD fallback and an audit record is appended — never both, never neither.* Three rejection predicates, all pure arithmetic/set logic over the decision object:

1. `size_pct > GUARDRAIL_LIMITS["max_position_pct"]` (default 0.10) → reject (`:149-150`)
2. `short_amount > available_cash` → reject (`:150-151`)
3. `rating ∉ {"Buy","Overweight","Hold","Underweight","Sell"}` → reject, fall back to REVIEW/HOLD (`:152-153`)

**Exact acceptance conditions a `test/offline/` test can check** (all with zero network, no LLM, no clock dependence):

| # | Condition | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| G1 | For each of the 3 predicates, a decision that violates it **at any margin** (including exactly at the boundary: `pct == 0.10` passes, `pct == 0.1000001` rejects) is **not** returned as executable. | `:149-153`, `:157` |
| G2 | Escape count over the whole generated adversarial matrix is **exactly 0**, asserted as arithmetic (`escapes == 0`), not as "no exception raised". | `:156-157` |
| G3 | Every rejected decision produces **exactly one** audit record, and that record names (a) which predicate fired, (b) the observed value, (c) the configured limit. | `:160-161`, `:167-168` |
| G4 | The returned decision after rejection is **a member of the legal 5-tier set** and its rating is `Hold`/`REVIEW`. | `:152-153`, `invariants.md:11` |
| G5 | The guardrail is a **pure function of (decision, limits)**: same inputs → byte-identical output and byte-identical audit record across two calls (a determinism assertion). | `:146` "deterministic" |
| G6 | Fuzz/property test over randomly generated decisions confirms `passed ∨ rejected-with-fallback` is exhaustive — no third code path. | `:153-154`, `invariants.md:8` |
| G7 | A negative test that **fails when the invariant is violated**: a monkeypatched guardrail that passes everything must make G2 fail. | `verification-constraints.md:8-9`, `.agent/rules.md:14-16` |

**Note on today's code:** `src/guardrail.py:4` already defines `GUARDRAIL_LIMITS = {"max_position_pct": 0.10, "max_short_pct_of_cash": 1.0}` and `VALID_RATINGS` (`:5`) but **no callable guardrail exists** — the module is a stub with no function, and `test/offline/test_guardrail.py:4-6` raises `NotImplementedError`. So the offline test currently **errors, not passes** — CI runs `pytest test/offline -m offline` (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:57-58`), so the gate is red today. Also note `pytest.ini` declares markers but **no test file carries `@pytest.mark.offline`**, so `-m offline` selects nothing (see A7).

##### 3b. REQ-TRACEABILITY — statements at `requirements.yaml:109-137`, ADR `adr/003-evidence-traceability.md:11-15`, invariant `invariants.md:10`

**Observable behaviour:** *every assertion classified as critical emits a link record* `assertion_id → referenced_data_snapshot_id`, *and each resolved snapshot carries `data_source` + `fetch_timestamp`; the final decision is walkable down to those snapshots and a trace table is renderable from the links.*

**Exact acceptance conditions** (deterministic, offline, in-memory fake store):

| # | Condition | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| T1 | Recording a critical assertion yields a link whose `assertion_id`, `referenced_data_snapshot_id`, `data_source`, `fetch_timestamp` are each non-empty and correctly typed. **0 missing fields** across the fixture set. | `:113-114`, `:121-122` |
| T2 | The link's `referenced_data_snapshot_id` **resolves** in the snapshot store — a dangling ID is a failure, not a warning. | `:123-125` |
| T3 | **Completeness is measured, not presumed:** count critical assertions in the fixture = N, count resolvable links = M, assert `M == N` (this is the check that makes "== 100%" non-vacuous). | `:121-122` |
| T4 | The auditor, run on the final decision, resolves **every** link it walks and returns `traceable == True`. | `:120`, `:125-126` |
| T5 | A renderable trace table is produced with one row per link and no empty cells. | `:125-126` |
| T6 | Storage-bounding clause is respected: a **non-critical** assertion may be omitted **without** making T3/T4 fail. | `:117-118` |
| T7 | Negative test: a recorder that drops one critical link must make T3 fail — proving T3 is a real gate. | `verification-constraints.md:8-9` |
| T8 | Determinism: a fixed fixture produces byte-identical link records on re-run (supports the point-in-time discipline in `memory-design.md:16`). | `memeroy-design.md:16` |

**Blocking prerequisite for T3**: "critical assertion" must be defined (A4). Until it is, T3 collapses to `0 == 0` and passes vacuously.

#### 4. Ambiguities, conflicts, and missing source links

##### Ambiguities

- **A1 — "tokens" is never defined** (`requirements.yaml:46`, `:48`). Characters ÷4? `tiktoken` on which model? Provider-reported? The budget 8000 (`:47`) is uncomparable to 6000 (`:50`) across tokenizers, and a test that measures differently from the instrumented runtime is meaningless.
- **A2 — "critical invariants and standing constraints survive re-injection"** (`:51-53`) has no metric and no threshold. Compare `docs/architecture/risk-list.md:8` which acknowledges it is "hard to prove in general". "Send a sentinel string through and assert it appears" is a possible operationalisation, but it is not what the text says.
- **A3 — `bull_position` / `bear_position` / `DIVERGENCE_THRESHOLD` are undefined** (`:87-90`), with no default for `DIVERGENCE_THRESHOLD` and no numeric field in the turn schema (`:78`, `src/structured_debater.py:3`) to compute them from. The convergence half of this requirement is currently untestable and unimplementable.
- **A4 — "critical assertion" is never defined** (`:117-118`, `:122`, ADR `003:14-15`, `invariants.md:10`). This is the determinative gap for REQ-TRACEABILITY. `risk-list.md:10` and `adr/003:26-27` both defer to "adjust the critical-assertion classification" without saying what the classification *is*.
- **A5 — "stalled progress" has no definition** (`:186`), unlike `REPEAT_THRESHOLD` (default 3, `:194`) and budget exhaustion.
- **A6 — "logged reason" vs "names the trigger"** (`:192` vs `:195-196`) are different assertions, and the set of legal trigger names is not enumerated, so T-style exact-string assertions are impossible.
- **A7 — "No hard cap exceeds the configurable max tool rounds"** (`:196-197`) — "max tool rounds" is attributed to `default_config.py` (`:63`) but that file **does not exist in this repository** (see S1), and it is ambiguous whether this constrains the debate round cap, the tool-round cap, or both.
- **A8 — "critical invariants" in `:51` vs the formal invariant register** — the phrase seems to mean something different from `docs/architecture/invariants.md`'s INV-* entries.

##### Conflicts

- **C1 — Type vocabulary vs stated drivers (the main finding).** `requirements.yaml:7` demands coverage of cost/governance/security; the registry supplies none (§2), while `architecture-blueprint.md:23-29` makes cost and safety the top-two drivers. **Conflict between the registry's own convention line and its content.**
- **C2 — `AGENTS.md:78` vs feasibility of a fit criterion.** "Every invariant has at least one test that **fails** when the invariant is violated" is fine for `INV-GUARDRAIL-ZERO-ESCAPE` and `INV-RATING-VALIDITY` (`invariants.md:8,11`) — but the same clause binds `INV-CONTEXT-BUDGET` (`:9`), whose violation is "faithfulness drops > 0.1" (`:53-54`), a **live evaluator** test that cannot live in `test/offline/` (`AGENTS.md:48`, `verification-constraints.md:21-23`). Offline determinism and that fit criterion are in direct tension. Needs a stubbed judge or a reworded criterion.
- **C3 — `INV-RATING-VALIDITY` exists in the register but has no requirement ID of its own** (`invariants.md:11`); it is attributed to REQ-HARD-GUARDRAIL, and it overlaps requirement clause (c) (`:152-153`). Same for `INV-GUARDRAIL-ZERO-ESCAPE`. Not a contradiction, but two invariants share one requirement and one test obligation (`AGENTS.md:78`) — so a test must be named for each invariant or coverage silently halves.
- **C4 — `REQ-HARD-GUARDRAIL`'s fallback is "REVIEW/HOLD"** (`:153`), but "REVIEW" is **not** in the legal 5-tier set (`:152`, `src/guardrail.py:5`). The fallback target is therefore itself outside the vocabulary it enforces, and `INV-RATING-VALIDITY` (`invariants.md:11`, "Final rating is always a member of the legal 5-tier set") would be **violated by its own documented fallback** unless "REVIEW/HOLD" is read as exactly `Hold`. This is a genuine contradiction between `requirements.yaml:153` and `invariants.md:11` and it will bite the test in §3a G4.
- **C5 — Triple module-mapping sources disagree on invariants.** `docs/code-governance/structural-constraints.md` maps `structured_debater.py` and `termination_controller.py` to "—" invariants, which matches `invariants.md` (which has no entry for them) but means two of five requirements have **no invariant** — consistent, but it undercuts `AGENTS.md:78`'s universal phrasing. No conflict, but note it.
- **C6 — `registry_notes.token_efficiency_requirements`** lists `REQ-STRUCTURED-DEBATE` (`:219`) although that requirement is typed `quality` (`:73`) and contains no token metric in its fit criterion (`:82-90`). Classification and note disagree.

##### Missing / broken source links

- **S1 — Every `source:` field cites files that are not in this repository.** All five (`:62-66`, `:99-103`, `:133-136`, `:169-174`, `:205-210`) reference `default_config.py`, `bull_researcher.py`, `conditional_logic.py`, `trading_graph.py`, `agents/trader` — none exist under `src/` (which contains only five stub modules). `requirements.yaml:10` requires that discovered requirements be "linked to sources"; the links point to an **external** repo (`AGENTS.md:11-12`) with a **branch-unpinned URL**, so nothing here can verify them. This is the most serious traceability defect in a document whose job is traceability.
- **S2 — No `source` cites an instructor note, PRD, or transcript** — all five trace to the same single source type ("analysed from existing system"). `transcripts/` is empty (`transcripts/README.md:8`) and the AI-use log is empty (`docs/ai-use-log.yaml:8`), so no discovery has an auditable origin.
- **S3 — Requirement ↔ ADR ↔ invariant links are one-directional.** `docs/architecture/trace-matrix.md:13` still says "(TODO: map every requirement … This table is a seed.)", and `verification-constraints.md:31` says "(TODO: add the concrete test-to-requirement mapping)". So the two artifacts that would let a grader verify §1–§3 are explicitly unfinished.
- **S4 — ADRs are all `Status: Proposed` with unfilled `Decision owner` / `Date`** (`adr/001:3-5`, `adr/003:3-5`, `adr/004:3-5`). `AGENTS.md:51` requires changes to `docs/architecture/*` to have an ADR — but ADR-004, which authorises the safety boundary, is not approved. Meanwhile `.agent/rules.md:17-19` requires human approval for changes to `src/guardrail.py`. **Building REQ-HARD-GUARDRAIL therefore requires approving ADR-004 first**; that is a human gate, not something I may do.
- **S5 — `req-schema.json` cannot detect any of the defects above.** `type` is a closed enum of strings (`:57-68`) with no cross-field rule; `additionalProperties: true` (`:100`) lets anything through; and `fit_criterion` is an unconstrained `string` (`:78-81`) — the schema **cannot tell** "bare prose" from "METRIC + THRESHOLD + VERIFY". So `fit_criterion_machine_checkable: true` (`:67`, `:104`, `:137`, `:175`, `:211`) is a **self-declaration the CI gate at `.github/workflows/ci.yml:15-34` never checks**. Adding a `pattern` requiring `METRIC:`/`THRESHOLD:` would make the gate real — but `requirements.yaml` and the schema both need an ADR to change (`AGENTS.md:52`).
- **S6 — `priority` enum is `"Wont"`** (`req-schema.json:84`) while the YAML convention writes "Won't" (`requirements.yaml:9`). Latent: no entry uses it today, so CI passes — but the apostrophe form would fail validation. Worth correcting on the next ADR.
- **S7 — CI offline gate is currently vacuous/red.** `pytest.ini` defines an `offline` marker, but no file in `test/offline/` applies it, so `pytest test/offline -m offline` (`ci.yml:58`) selects **zero tests**; and each existing offline test raises `NotImplementedError` (`test_offline/test_guardrail.py:6`, `test_context_budget.py`, `test_termination.py`). So "zero adversarial escapes" (`:157`) is **unverified today**, and the "gate" at `ci.yml:58` would pass empty.
- **S8 — `verification-constraints.md:18-19` sets "faithfulness / relevancy ≥ 0.6"** for the "AI-generated explanation layer" — but **no requirement in the registry mentions an explanation layer**, so this verification obligation is orphaned (inverse of the S3 gap).
- **S9 — `Prompt.md:55-56` / `.opencode/rules.md:12` / `ci.yml:64-77`** mandate the AI-use log, and `docs/ai-use-log.yaml:8` is `entries: []`. This review session itself will need a log entry (`transcripts/README.md:3-5`), which I am not writing because you asked me not to modify files.

#### C. In-scope acceptance conditions (approved, with pinned decisions)

Basis: sections 3a/3b of the review were approved. The pinned specifics are incorporated **verbatim as the binding values**; unsupported readings are removed.

##### C.1 REQ-HARD-GUARDRAIL (`requirements.yaml:142-175`; ADR `adr/004-hard-guardrail.md:12-15`; `invariants.md:8,11`)

**Observable behaviour:** a decision object is either passed through unchanged, or replaced by a fallback decision with audit action `"REVIEW/HOLD"` plus exactly one audit record — never both, never neither.

**Pinned values:**
- **Position:** accept `size_pct <= max_position_pct`; reject `size_pct > max_position_pct`. Default `max_position_pct = 0.10`; **exactly 10.0% is accepted**. Configurable (`src/guardrail.py:4`).
- **Short:** accept `short_amount == available_cash`; reject `short_amount > available_cash`. (`src/guardrail.py:4` `max_short_pct_of_cash = 1.0`.) *Interpretation note:* at `cash == 0`, `short == cash == 0` is accepted by this rule; the test must use a non-zero cash fixture to exercise the accept-at-equality case, and I flag this as the one arithmetic edge worth confirming at test-authoring time.
- **Ratings:** membership is tested against the exact case-sensitive set `{Buy, Overweight, Hold, Underweight, Sell}` — no trimming, no case folding, no aliases (`src/guardrail.py:5`).
- **Fallback:** rating `"Hold"`; audit action `"REVIEW/HOLD"`.
- **Purity:** pure deterministic function; no LLM/network imports; no clock dependence.

**Acceptance conditions (deterministic, `test/offline/`):**

| # | Condition |
|---|---|
| G1 | Boundary matrix on position: `9.9999…`, **`0.10` accepted**; `0.10 + ε` rejected. Same shape for short: `short == cash` accepted, `short > cash` rejected. |
| G2 | Rating matrix: each of the five exact strings accepted; `"buy"`, `"HOLD "`, `"Review"`, `""`, `None`, non-string → rejected with fallback. |
| G3 | **Zero escapes** asserted arithmetically (`escapes == 0`) over the full generated crossing matrix — not "no exception raised". |
| G4 | Every rejection returns rating `"Hold"` (a member of the legal set, satisfying `invariants.md:11`) and action string `"REVIEW/HOLD"`. The fallback rating **must not** be the literal `"REVIEW"`. |
| G5 | Exactly **one** audit record per rejection, naming (a) trigger, (b) observed value, (c) configured limit. Zero records on pass-through. |
| G6 | Determinism: two calls on identical input produce byte-identical decision and byte-identical audit record. |
| G7 | Source-hygiene assertion: the guardrail module's imports contain no network/LLM/clock module (structural check over `sys.modules`/AST). |
| G8 | Configurability: reloading with `max_position_pct = 0.20` shifts the accept boundary to exactly 0.20. |
| G9 | **Negative test:** a guardrail patched to always pass **must** fail G3 — proving G3 is a real gate (`verification-constraints.md:8-9`). |

##### C.2 REQ-TRACEABILITY (`requirements.yaml:109-137`; ADR `adr/003-evidence-traceability.md:11-15`; `invariants.md:10`)

**Observable behaviour:** every assertion flagged `critical=True` by the producing agent yields a link `assertion_id → referenced_data_snapshot_id`; each snapshot carries `data_source` and a UTC ISO-8601 `fetch_timestamp`; the final decision references at least one evidence snapshot; `audit()` walks and resolves the chain; `render_table()` produces a renderable table.

**Pinned values:**
- **Critical** = explicitly flagged `critical=True` by the producing agent. Unflagged ⇒ non-critical ⇒ link optional, may be omitted.
- **Fields:** `assertion_id`, `referenced_data_snapshot_id`, `data_source`, `fetch_timestamp` (UTC ISO-8601, `datetime.fromisoformat`-parseable, tz-aware).
- **API:** `TraceRecorder` in memory only, with `audit()` and `render_table()`. **Persistence deferred.**
- **Floor:** the final decision must reference **at least one** evidence snapshot.

**Acceptance conditions:**

| # | Condition |
|---|---|
| T1 | Every recorded critical link has all four fields non-empty and correctly typed; **0 missing fields** across the fixture set. |
| T2 | Every `referenced_data_snapshot_id` **resolves** in the in-memory store; a dangling ID fails. |
| T3 | **Measured completeness:** N = critical-flagged assertions in the fixture, M = resolvable links; assert `M == N` — the form that makes "== 100%" (`:122`) non-vacuous. |
| T4 | `audit()` on a final decision returns traceable, having resolved every visited link; a decision with zero referenced snapshots **fails** the at-least-one floor. |
| T5 | `render_table()` yields one row per link, no empty cells. |
| T6 | Non-critical (unflagged) assertions may be omitted **without** failing T3 or T4. |
| T7 | Timestamp format: every `fetch_timestamp` round-trips through `fromisoformat` and is tz-aware UTC. |
| T8 | Determinism: fixed fixture ⇒ byte-identical link records across two recorder instances. |
| T9 | **Negative test:** a recorder that drops one critical link **must** fail T3. |

**Declared but not asserted (kept out of the gate, per your pinning):** T2-of-the-review's snapshot-store persistence, cross-run retention, and point-in-time filtering (`memory-design.md:16`) are **not** offline-testable in-memory and are deferred with persistence.

#### E. Risks to the offline test plan

1. **The offline gate is vacuous or red today — highest risk.** `ci.yml:58` runs `pytest test/offline -m offline`, but **no test file applies the `offline` marker** (see `pytest.ini` marker declaration only), so the selection is empty; and every existing offline test raises `NotImplementedError` (`test/offline/test_guardrail.py:6`, `test_context_budget.py`, `test_termination.py`). A green CI run would therefore prove nothing. Tests must be written marker-first.
2. **There is nothing to test yet.** `src/guardrail.py` declares constants (`:4-5`) but **no callable**; `src/trace_recorder.py:1` is a docstring only. The approved conditions specify a pure function and an in-memory recorder — both must be built from zero, so G1-G9 / T1-T9 cannot run until then. Note the covenant requires a **negative test per feature** (`.agent/rules.md:14-16`), which G9 and T9 provide.
3. **Negative tests are patch-shaped, so they need a seam.** G9 and T9 monkeypatch behaviour; without a clean injection point the "negative test" degrades into testing the monkeypatch. The pure-function and in-memory designs you pinned help, but the seam must be named deliberately.
4. **No test-to-requirement mapping exists yet**, so `AGENTS.md:77` and `verification-constraints.md:7` are unenforced — a test could silently miss a fit criterion. `verification-constraints.md:31` is still a TODO.
5. **ADR-004 is unapproved**, so the guardrail tests will, for now, run against a design nobody has signed off. `.agent/rules.md:17-19` blocks the *change*; the *tests* can be drafted, but they encode a decision the architecture session may still revise — churn risk on G1-G8. Pre-the-hand, `trace-matrix.md` maps the guardrail to "offline test: zero adversarial escapes" (`:10`), matching G3; no equivalent row is at risk for traceability beyond `:9`.
6. **C4's residual wording risk:** if an implementer reads `requirements.yaml:153` or `runtime-policy-catalog.md:7` literally and emits rating `"REVIEW"`, G4 and INV-RATING-VALIDITY both fail. The pinned decision is in this note only — it is **not** in any file the implementer reads. Expect at least one correction cycle unless the three stale strings are clarified at the next ADR.
7. **Short-rule zero-cash edge:** the pinned "accept `short == cash`, reject `short > cash`" makes `short == cash == 0` acceptable. A fixture set that includes zero cash will look like a guardrail hole to a reviewer even though it follows the rule. Confirm the intended semantics before authoring the fixture; this is the one place where I recommend a confirmation rather than a silent choice.
8. **Determinism holds only if timestamps are injected.** T8 and G6 assert byte-identity, but `fetch_timestamp` is a value the recorder must not take from the clock inside the asserted path; the fixture must supply it. Otherwise T8 is flaky — a CI-blocking flake in a safety-critical suite.
9. **Scope creep at authoring time:** `REQ-CONTEXT-BUDGET` and `REQ-TERMINATION-DISCIPLINE` tests exist as stubs and are red (`test/offline/test_context_budget.py`, `test_termination.py`). Fixing them to get CI green would silently pull out-of-scope work into this cycle and collide with B's pending relabels.

### D2 Architecture — Candidate Generation and Evaluation

#### 0. Authority basis and one blocking conflict I must surface first

**Authority used.** `architecture-blueprint.md:3-8` is master; `.agent/rules.md:17-19` requires an ADR **plus human approval** to touch `src/guardrail.py`; ADR-004 is `Status: Proposed` (`docs/architecture/adr/004-hard-guardrail.md:3`). So this session can *recommend* approval, not grant it — approval is your act.

**CONFLICT (surface, do not proceed).** `.opencode/rules.md:4` forbids non-agentic modification of code, and `docs/architecture/permission-model.md:16-17` grants root RW on `src/**` and `test/**` — but `.agent/rules.md:17-19` and `AGENTS.md:94-95` make `src/guardrail.py` a gated path. The two are compatible only if the ADR is approved *before* `src/guardrail.py` is written. If you approve the ADRs and then want the guardrail written in the build session, that is consistent. If you approve the ADRs but keep the build session read-only on `src/guardrail.py`, the guardrail stays unbuilt and `test/offline/test_guardrail.py:4-6` keeps CI red (see §2.1). I flag it rather than resolve it.

**Second conflict, pre-existing and material to scoring.** `.github/workflows/ci.yml:58` runs `pytest test/offline -m offline`, but `pytest.ini:2-4` only *declares* the marker and **no test file carries `@pytest.mark.offline`** (I grepped: zero matches in `test/`). With `--strict-markers` (`pytest.ini:5`) this selects **nothing**. So today the "zero escapes" gate (`docs/architecture/trace-matrix.md:10`) is vacuous, and any candidate I recommend inherits the obligation to fix the marker selection. `ci.yml:60` (`pytest -m "offline"`) has the same emptiness.

**Facts that bound every candidate.** `src/guardrail.py:1-5` is constants only (no callable); `src/trace_recorder.py:1` is one docstring line; no recorder test exists at all (`test/offline/` = `test_guardrail.py`, `test_context_budget.py`, `test_termination.py` only). Runtime is Python 3.11 in CI (`ci.yml:21`, `:54`) while the local interpreter is 3.14.7 (my probe) — so `datetime.fromisoformat` with a `Z` suffix is available in both, and `dataclasses.dataclass(slots=True)` (3.10+) is available. `pydantic` **is** present transitively via `langchain-openai>=1.6.6` (`requirements.txt:7`, probed as pydantic 2.13.4) but is **not a declared dependency** of ours. `requests>=2.32.4` is declared (`requirements.txt:14`) — relevant because a source-hygiene test must prove the guardrail does not transitively import it.

#### 1. Candidates

##### 1.A REQ-HARD-GUARDRAIL — five candidates

All candidates share the pinned semantics (`requirements.yaml:149-153` as narrowed by your session-1 pins at `transcripts/60760270-CUIHaoyu-01-requirements-classification.md:1240-1248`): accept `size_pct <= 0.10` and reject `> 0.10`; accept `short == cash`, reject `short > cash`; exact case-sensitive 5-tier membership (`src/guardrail.py:5`); fallback rating `"Hold"` + audit action `"REVIEW/HOLD"`; exactly one audit record per rejection naming trigger/observed/limit; no LLM, network, or clock.

They differ only in **where the enforcement choke point lives** and **what the check consumes**.

###### G-A — Single pure predicate function over a typed decision, returning a result object
**Boundaries.** One module `src/guardrail.py`; one public callable; no state; no I/O. Constants stay where they are (`src/guardrail.py:4-5`) and become the default of an injected limits argument.
**Data model.** Frozen `Decision` input (rating, size_pct, short_amount, available_cash, optional instrument_id); frozen `GuardrailResult` output (executable decision, `passed`, `audit: AuditRecord | None`). `AuditRecord` carries `trigger`, `observed`, `limit`, `action="REVIEW/HOLD"`, and a `record_id`.
**Control flow.** Evaluate the three predicates in a fixed, documented order; on the first violation, build exactly one `AuditRecord` and return the fallback decision; on no violation, return the input unchanged with `audit=None`. Ordering is observable, so it must be pinned or the audit record becomes nondeterministic when several predicates fire at once (**this is a real defect in the pinned design — see §6, risk R3**).
**Failure/fallback.** Rejection → fallback decision + one record (satisfies `invariants.md:8,11` and `runtime-policy-catalog.md:7`). Malformed input (missing field, `NaN`, non-numeric) is a *fourth* case the pins do not cover; the fail-closed treatment (treat as rejection with trigger `MALFORMED_DECISION`) is a decision that needs your sign-off.
**Pins.** Satisfies all: pure, no clock, no LLM/network, one record, exact boundary arithmetic is trivially expressible.

###### G-B — Policy-object guardrail: ordered list of `(predicate, trigger_name, limit_key)` rule objects
**Boundaries.** Same single module, but the three checks are data (a tuple registry) rather than code. Public surface identical to G-A.
**Data model.** `RULE_SET: tuple[Rule, ...]`, each `Rule(predicate: Callable[[Decision, Limits], bool], trigger: Trigger, limit_key: str)`. Adding a fourth limit (e.g. a crypto position cap anticipated by `risk-list.md:7`) means appending a row, not editing control flow.
**Control flow.** Iterate the rule set in order; first match wins → one record.
**Failure/fallback.** Identical to G-A.
**Pins.** Satisfies all, with one advantage: "configurable limits" (`requirements.yaml:166`, `risk-list.md:7`) becomes a data edit. One disadvantage: a rule table is inspectable *data*, and a table can be mutated at runtime — so a test must assert immutability, or the "signature" claim silently weakens.

###### G-C — Execution-boundary chokepoint: guardrail is called *by* a single `execute()` wrapper that no caller can bypass
**Boundaries.** `src/guardrail.py` holds the predicate; a thin `execute_decision()` wrapper refuses to return anything the guardrail did not stamp with a signed result token. The AI path can only reach the simulated exchange (`architecture-blueprint.md:34-37`) through this wrapper.
**Data model.** G-A's model plus a `stamped: bool`/nonce on the result; the wrapper consumes the stamp once.
**Control flow.** Decision → guardrail → stamped result → wrapper → exchange.
**Failure/fallback.** Fail-closed: no stamp, no execution.
**Pins.** Strongest zero-escape *structurally*, but it needs the execution path to exist. **It does not exist in this repository**: `src/` has five stubs and no order-execution module at all (`src/` listing), and `requirements.yaml:169-174` sources the agent pipeline to files absent here. So this candidate's central mechanism is untestable offline today — it would be tested by a mock wrapper, which proves nothing about the real choke point.

###### G-D — Post-hoc verifier over the rendered final JSON state
**Boundaries.** No callable guardrail at decision time; a separate validator walks the final state JSON (`architecture-blueprint.md:96-97`) after the run and flags violations.
**Control flow.** Run completes → state written → validator flags.
**Failure/fallback.** Cannot prevent an escape; only reports it after the fact.
**Pins.** **Violates the core pin.** `requirements.yaml:145-147` requires the check *before* it reaches the execution path, and `THRESHOLD: == 0` (`:157`) counts escapes past the guardrail. A post-hoc verifier has an escape count equal to the number of violations it finds, i.e. > 0. Rejected outright.

###### G-E — LLM-as-judge guardrail with a deterministic wrapper
**Boundaries.** A model call classifies the decision with a prompt; a regex/arith wrapper polices the model's answer.
**Failure/fallback.** Nondeterministic; network-dependent; clock/replay dependent.
**Pins.** **Violates** "pure deterministic function; no LLM/network imports; no clock dependence" (your pin at `transcript:1244`; `requirements.yaml:146` "deterministic"; `test/offline/` must need no API per `verification-constraints.md:22`). Also violates `architecture-blueprint.md:89-90` intent (zero safety escapes cannot be measured when the checker itself is stochastic). Rejected. Note it is *already* rejected in two places: `adr/004-hard-guardrail.md:19` ("Soft prompt-based boundary — not enforced deterministically") and `option-ledger.md:8`.

##### 1.B REQ-TRACEABILITY — five candidates

All share the pins (transcript `:1245-1248`): fields `assertion_id`, `referenced_data_snapshot_id`, `data_source`, `fetch_timestamp` (UTC ISO-8601, parseable); in-memory; `audit()` and `render_table()`; persistence deferred; final decision references ≥1 snapshot; determinism.

###### T-A — In-memory recorder with explicit `critical=True` flag and a resolve-by-lookup store
**Boundaries.** One module `src/trace_recorder.py`. Two record kinds: `DataSnapshot` and `TraceLink`. A `TraceRecorder` holding two append-only lists plus a `final_decision_refs` set.
**Data model.** `DataSnapshot(snapshot_id, data_source, fetch_timestamp)`; `TraceLink(link_id, assertion_id, referenced_data_snapshot_id, critical: bool)`. The four pinned fields are split across the two records — `data_source`/`fetch_timestamp` live on the snapshot, and the link carries the foreign key. This is exactly the chain shape in `requirements.yaml:113-114`.
**Control flow.** Producer calls `record_snapshot(...)` when it fetches data; producer calls `record_assertion(assertion, critical=True/False, snapshot_id=...)`; PM calls `record_final_decision(decision_id, refs=[snapshot_id...])`; auditor calls `audit()`; renderer calls `render_table()`.
**Failure/fallback.** Dangling `snapshot_id` → the link records the attempt and `audit()` reports it as unresolved (a gap, not a silent drop) — matches `invariants.md:10` operational fallback "Log gap + surface in review memo". Zero refs on the final decision → `audit()` returns not-traceable.
**Pins.** Satisfies all. `data_source`/`fetch_timestamp` are **supplied**, never read from the clock — which is what makes determinism (T8 in `transcript:1357`) honest.

###### T-B — Snapshot-first recorder: timestamps are *validated* at snapshot creation, source is an enum
**Boundaries.** Same module, but `record_snapshot` rejects an unparseable or non-UTC timestamp at creation rather than at audit time, and `data_source` is restricted to a declared enumeration of vendor names.
**Data model.** `DataSnapshot` with `data_source: DataSource` (enum: yfinance/FRED/SEC/Polymarket per `architecture-blueprint.md:34-35`) and `fetch_timestamp: str` validated by `datetime.fromisoformat` + `tzinfo is not None` + offset zero.
**Control flow.** Fail-fast at record time.
**Failure/fallback.** Invalid timestamp → raises a typed `TraceError` at record time; the run's policy catalog has no row for this today (`runtime-policy-catalog.md:5-14` has no trace row at all — a gap in that catalog).
**Pins.** Satisfies all, and *strengthens* the parseability pin. The cost is the enum: an undecided vendor list becomes a source of false rejections and a migration hazard the moment someone adds a data vendor. `risk-list.md` has no row for this.

###### T-C — Persisted recorder backed by the existing memory log / SQLite checkpoint
**Boundaries.** Writes links into `~/.tradingagents/memory/trading_memory.md` or a per-ticker SQLite DB (`memory-design.md:6-11`).
**Pins.** **Contradicts your pin** ("in-memory… persistence deferred", transcript `:1246`). Also: memory log is append-only and pruned (`memory-design.md:14`, `:22` retention is a TODO), so retention would silently delete audit evidence; and file/SQLite access makes the offline determinism test flaky (`verification-constraints.md:22`). Rejected, but this is the natural *successor*, not a bad design.

###### T-D — Per-token / full-provenance recorder
**Boundaries.** Every token of every agent message linked to a snapshot.
**Pins.** **Already rejected twice**: `option-ledger.md:10` ("Per-token full provenance — Too heavy") and `adr/003-evidence-traceability.md:19`. Violates nothing in your pins but blows the storage bound that `adr/003:23` and `risk-list.md:10` both worry about, and produces no extra audit value past `critical=True`.

###### T-E — Decorator / context-manager instrumentation on the analyst functions
**Boundaries.** A `@traced` decorator wraps each analyst call and auto-links whatever snapshot the analyst touched.
**Data model.** Implicit; links are derived from a ambient per-call context, not passed explicitly.
**Control flow.** Ambient context is set at call entry, read by the decorator at exit.
**Pins.** Satisfies the fields but **fails the `critical=True` pin**: your definition (transcript `:1231`, `:1341`) makes criticality an *explicit flag set by the producing agent*. A decorator infers rather than receives, so "explicitly flagged" becomes "heuristically attributed", and the measurable-completeness assertion (T3, `transcript:1352`) becomes a measurement of the decorator, not the agent. Also ambient state is the classic determinism hazard across two recorder instances (T8). Rejected.

#### 2. Weighted scoring

##### 2.1 Weights and their justification

I derive weights from the repository, not from preference. Ordering evidence is cited per weight.

| Driver | Weight | Why this weight (evidence) |
|---|---|---|
| Safety / zero-escape | **0.30** | It is the only driver with a zero-tolerance numeric threshold: `METRIC: adversarial_escapes_past_guardrail; THRESHOLD: == 0` (`requirements.yaml:155-157`), typed `invariant` (`:143`), registered twice (`invariants.md:8`, `:11`), and given its own change gate (`.agent/rules.md:17-19`, `architecture-blueprint.md:104-107`). No other driver is gated that hard. |
| Auditability | **0.25** | Two requirements depend on it (REQ-TRACEABILITY `requirements.yaml:109-137`, plus the guardrail's own "exactly one audit record" pin `:167-168`), and `architecture-blueprint.md:94-99` makes trace exposure an observability obligation. Second-highest because it is *the* stated reason the project exists (`:27`). |
| Testability / offline determinism | **0.20** | Hard precondition for anything shipping: CI runs offline only (`ci.yml:57-60`), `test/offline/` must need no API (`verification-constraints.md:22`), every invariant needs a test that fails on violation (`AGENTS.md:78`), and every feature needs a negative test (`.agent/rules.md:14-16`). High, but it is an enabler of the first two rather than an end. |
| Token/runtime efficiency | **0.10** | Driver #1 in the blueprint (`architecture-blueprint.md:23-24`) but **not in scope this cycle** (your scope pin) and, for these two components, near-zero by construction — neither calls an LLM. It is scored because a candidate *could* regress it (e.g. T-D bloat). |
| Maintainability | **0.10** | Carries real obligations — one element ↔ one module (`structural-constraints.md:18`), header docstrings referencing ADR/REQ/INV (`:20-21`), no internals access (`.agent/rules.md:8-10`) — but these are satisfied by all viable candidates, so it discriminates weakly. |

Weighted above efficiency/maintainability for that reason. |

Sums to 1.00. Scores are 1-5 (5 best; for migration risk, **5 = lowest risk**).

| Candidate | Safety .30 | Audit .25 | Test/offline .20 | Efficiency .10 | Maintain .10 | Migr. risk .15 | **Weighted** |

| **G-A** typed pure predicate | 5 | 5 | 5 | 5 | 4 | 5 | **4.85** |
| G-B rule-table policy | 4 | 5 | 5 | 5 | 5 | 4 | **4.65** |

Evidence behind the non-obvious cells:

- **G-A safety = 5, G-B = 4.** G-B's rule set is mutable data; `src/guardrail.py:4` already publishes `GUARDRAIL_LIMITS` as a plain module dict, so a table-shaped design invites runtime mutation of the enforcement set. G-A's limits are a frozen default argument, so the *only* way to change the boundary is to pass different limits — which is exactly the configurability `requirements.yaml:166` permits and `transcript:1333` (G8) requires to be observable.
- **G-A/G-B auditability = 5.** Both emit exactly one structured record with the three pinned fields (`requirements.yaml:167-168`), and both make `render_table`-style inspection trivial. The tie-break for G-A is that a *typed* record refuses to be built with a missing field, so "exactly one record naming trigger/observed/limit" is structurally guaranteed rather than tested into.
- **G-C safety = 5 but testability = 1.** There is no execution module in `src/` and no exchange adapter, and `requirements.yaml:169-174` traces the decision site to `trading_graph.py` / `agents/trader`, neither of which exists here. Any test of G-C is a test of a mock, so its "zero escape" score is unproven — which under `verification-constraints.md:8-9` (the test must *fail* when violated) means the invariant is untestable at the stated threshold.
- **G-D safety = 1.** `requirements.yaml:145-147` demands the check *before* execution; a post-hoc verifier by construction has escapes ≥ the violations it finds, contradicting `THRESHOLD: == 0` (`:157`).
- **G-E efficiency = 1 / testability = 1.** Adds an LLM call per decision (against driver #1, `architecture-blueprint.md:23-24`), and `verification-constraints.md:22` forbids API dependence in `test/offline/`.
- **G-A migration = 5.** It adds a callable to a module that today exposes only constants (`src/guardrail.py:1-5`); nothing that exists is removed, satisfying "extend, never replace" (`AGENTS.md:36-38`, `structural-constraints.md:19`). G-C would require adding a choke point *ahead* of a pipeline that does not exist here (migration = 1).

##### 4.1 ADR-004 — `docs/architecture/adr/004-hard-guardrail.md`

**Status:** `Proposed` → **`Accepted (pending human sign-off)`**. Line 3 changes to `- **Status:** Accepted` only after you sign; until then it is `Accepted (pending sign-off)` and `src/guardrail.py` stays read-only per `.agent/rules.md:17-19`. **Decision owner:** fill with your name (line 4). **Date:** 2026-11-24 (line 5).

**Context — append (after line 10):** add the fact that `src/guardrail.py:1-5` contains constants only, and that the three pinned boundary semantics are fixed at 10.0% inclusive / short ≤ cash / exact case-sensitive tier set.

**Decision — replace lines 12-15 with:**
> Introduce `Guardrail` as a single **pure function** in `src/guardrail.py`: `evaluate_decision(decision, limits=DEFAULT_LIMITS) -> GuardrailResult`. It hard-checks every decision before it can reach execution: `size_pct > max_position_pct` (default `0.10`, **exactly 0.10 accepted**) → reject; `short_amount > available_cash` (**exactly equal accepted**) → reject; `rating` not an exact case-sensitive member of `{Buy, Overweight, Hold, Underweight, Sell}` → reject. Every rejection returns a decision whose rating is `"Hold"` with audit action `"REVIEW/HOLD"` (**`"REVIEW"` is never a rating**) and exactly **one** audit record naming `trigger`, `observed_value`, `configured_limit`. Multiple simultaneous violations resolve by a declared, fixed trigger precedence. The function reads no clock, imports no LLM/network module, and holds no mutable state. Zero tolerance: `adversarial_escapes_past_guardrail == 0`.
> **Declared scope limit:** the function guards the decision *object*. The structural chokepoint that forces all execution through it is deferred because no execution module exists in this repository; it is tracked as a consequence below.

**Alternatives considered — replace lines 17-19 with the five from §1.A** (add G-C chokepoint, G-D post-hoc verifier, keep G-B rule table as "considered, rejected on mutable-enforcement grounds" and G-E as "rejected").

**Consequences — replace lines 21-24 with:**
> - Satisfies REQ-HARD-GUARDRAIL and INV-GUARDRAIL-ZERO-ESCAPE / INV-RATING-VALIDITY, offline and deterministically.
> - **Residual risk (must be tracked, not hidden):** the guardrail is a *library call*, not a structural choke point. "No escape" therefore means "every caller that invokes it obeys it". Until G-C lands, the zero-escape gate tests honouring callers, not the impossibility of bypass. This is the honest reading of `INV-GUARDRAIL-ZERO-ESCAPE` (`invariants.md:8`) today.
> - Conservative guardrail may reject a legitimate aggressive decision; limits are configurable so tuning needs no code change (`risk-list.md:7`, reopen condition below).
> - Malformed/non-numeric input is fail-closed (treated as a rejection). *(Needs your ratification — §6, R2.)*

**Reopen conditions — replace lines 26-28 with:**
> - Measured false-rejection rate too high, or a legitimate decision is blocked → tune `max_position_pct` / short policy (this is the existing condition, retained verbatim from `:26-27`).
> - **New asset class** (crypto, leveraged book) where 10%/cash semantics differ → `risk-list.md:7`.
> - **Any execution module appears** → this ADR's declared scope limit expires; adopt G-C.
> - **Any nightly/property fuzz surfaces an escape** → re-open immediately, not at next review.

##### 4.2 ADR-003 — `docs/architecture/adr/003-evidence-traceability.md`

**Status:** `Proposed` → **`Accepted (pending human sign-off)`** (line 3). Owner/Date: lines 4-5.

## 5.1 `src/guardrail.py` — ADR-004, REQ-HARD-GUARDRAIL, INV-GUARDRAIL-ZERO-ESCAPE, INV-RATING-VALIDITY

```python
### Existing, retained unchanged (src/guardrail.py:4-5)
GUARDRAIL_LIMITS: Final = {"max_position_pct": 0.10, "max_short_pct_of_cash": 1.0}
VALID_RATINGS: Final = frozenset({"Buy", "Overweight", "Hold", "Underweight", "Sell"})
### NOTE: `max_short_pct_of_cash: 1.0` (src/guardrail.py:4) corresponds to
### "short == available cash" -> the implementation must NOT read this name as a
### percentage of cash. See §6 R4 (naming).

FALLBACK_RATING: Final = "Hold"          # pin: transcript:1243; satisfies invariants.md:11
AUDIT_ACTION_REVIEW_HOLD: Final = "REVIEW/HOLD"   # pin: transcript:1243

class Trigger(str, Enum):                 # frozen vocabulary — audit records name these
    POSITION_LIMIT = "POSITION_LIMIT"     # size_pct > max_position_pct
    SHORT_EXCEEDS_CASH = "SHORT_EXCEEDS_CASH"
    ILLEGAL_RATING = "ILLEGAL_RATING"
    MALFORMED_DECISION = "MALFORMED_DECISION"   # fail-closed; see §6 R2

TRIGGER_PRECEDENCE: Final = (             # deterministic resolution when >1 fires (§6 R3)
    Trigger.MALFORMED_DECISION, Trigger.ILLEGAL_RATING,
    Trigger.POSITION_LIMIT, Trigger.SHORT_EXCEEDS_CASH,
)

@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class GuardrailLimits:
    max_position_pct: float = 0.10
    max_short_pct_of_cash: float = 1.0
    def as_dict(self) -> dict[str, float]: ...   # byte-identical serialisation

@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Decision:
    rating: str
    size_pct: float
    short_amount: float
    available_cash: float
    instrument_id: str | None = None
    # No timestamp field. A clock field would break determinism (transcript:1244, 1247).

@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class AuditRecord:
    record_id: str               # content-derived, NOT a counter/UUID (§6 R5)
    trigger: Trigger
    observed_value: object       # the offending observed number/rating, verbatim
    configured_limit: object     # the limit it was compared against, verbatim
    action: str = AUDIT_ACTION_REVIEW_HOLD
    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, object]: ...  # stable key order

@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class GuardrailResult:
    decision: Decision           # unchanged input on pass; FALLBACK_RATING decision on reject
    passed: bool
    audit: AuditRecord | None    # exactly one iff not passed (§6 R6)

def evaluate_decision(
    decision: Decision, limits: GuardrailLimits = GuardrailLimits()
) -> GuardrailResult: ...
```

**Contract clauses to freeze with the signatures.**
1. `passed is True` ⟺ `audit is None` **and** returned decision is the input unchanged.
2. `passed is False` ⟹ exactly one `AuditRecord` and `result.decision.rating == "Hold"`.
3. Boundary inclusive at 10.0% and at short == cash (`transcript:1240-1241`).
4. No module-level mutable state; `evaluate_decision` is referentially transparent.
5. Module imports restricted to `dataclasses`, `enum`, `typing`, `math` — enforced by a structural test (§6 R7).

## 5.2 `src/trace_recorder.py` — ADR-003, REQ-TRACEABILITY, INV-TRACE-COMPLETENESS

```python
### Data model — two record kinds (requirements.yaml:113-114 chain shape)
@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class DataSnapshot:
    snapshot_id: str            # caller-supplied, unique within a recorder
    data_source: str            # free text, NOT an enum (§3.2 rejected T-B)
    fetch_timestamp: str        # UTC ISO-8601, fromisoformat-parseable,
                                # tz-aware with explicit UTC offset (transcript:1245)

@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class TraceLink:
    link_id: str                # content-derived (§6 R5)
    assertion_id: str
    referenced_data_snapshot_id: str
    critical: bool              # explicit flag only (transcript:1231, 1341)

@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class AuditFinding:
    assertion_id: str
    reason: str                 # e.g. "DANGLING_SNAPSHOT", "MISSING_LINK"
    referenced_data_snapshot_id: str | None

@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class AuditReport:
    traceable: bool
    checked_links: int
    resolved_links: int
    findings: tuple[AuditFinding, ...]   # empty iff traceable
    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, object]: ...

class TraceRecorder:
    def record_snapshot(self, *, snapshot_id: str, data_source: str,
                        fetch_timestamp: str) -> DataSnapshot: ...
    def record_assertion(self, *, assertion_id: str, critical: bool,
                         referenced_data_snapshot_id: str) -> TraceLink: ...
    def record_final_decision(self, *, decision_id: str,
                              referenced_snapshot_ids: Sequence[str]) -> None: ...
    def audit(self) -> AuditReport: ...
    def render_table(self) -> list[dict[str, str]]: ...
```

**Contract clauses to freeze.**
1. `record_snapshot` validates the timestamp format and UTC offset and raises `TraceError` on violation — this is the **only** failure path and it needs a `runtime-policy-catalog.md` row (§4.2 consequences).
2. `record_assertion` never silently drops; a link to an unknown `snapshot_id` is stored and surfaces in `audit()` as `DANGLING_SNAPSHOT`.
3. `audit()` counts `M == N` over critical links (`requirements.yaml:121-122`, `transcript:1352`); `traceable` requires `M == N` **and** ≥1 referenced snapshot on the final decision (`transcript:1344`).
4. `render_table()` returns one row per link with every field present and non-empty (`transcript:1354`); row order is insertion order (deterministic).
5. The recorder never calls `datetime.now`/`time.time`/`uuid4` — all IDs and timestamps are either caller-supplied or content-derived.

# Memory / State Design

> What state survives across sessions, interruptions, and versions.

## Survives across sessions / versions
- **Memory log:** past decisions and their settlement reflections
  (`~/.tradingagents/memory/trading_memory.md`), loaded for the Portfolio
  Manager (point-in-time as of the trade date).
- **Checkpoints:** per-ticker SQLite (`~/.tradingagents/cache/checkpoints/*.db`)
  for resume, cleared on successful completion.
- **Run reports and state JSON:** under `results_dir`.

## Write & retrieval policy
- Memory log is append-only; each completed run appends its decision.
- Settlement fetches the realised return and generates a reflection per decision.
- Retrieval filters lessons by the trade date (point-in-time) for historical runs.

#### 2. Interface contract (frozen)

##### 2.1 `src/guardrail.py` — ADR-004 / REQ-HARD-GUARDRAIL / INV-GUARDRAIL-ZERO-ESCAPE / INV-RATING-VALIDITY

**Retained unchanged (extend, do not replace):**
```python
GUARDRAIL_LIMITS = {"max_position_pct": 0.10, "max_short_pct_of_cash": 1.0}
VALID_RATINGS = {"Buy", "Overweight", "Hold", "Underweight", "Sell"}
```
Exactly these two names keep their spelling, type and values. `VALID_RATINGS` stays a `set` (the architecture sketch proposed `frozenset`; I keep `set` to honour "do not replace", and mutate nothing at runtime — asserted by G7's module-state check).

**Additions:**
```python
FALLBACK_RATING: str = "Hold"                      # legal 5-tier member, never "REVIEW"
AUDIT_ACTION_REVIEW_HOLD: str = "REVIEW/HOLD"

class Trigger(str, Enum):
    MALFORMED_DECISION = "MALFORMED_DECISION"
    ILLEGAL_RATING = "ILLEGAL_RATING"
    POSITION_LIMIT = "POSITION_LIMIT"
    SHORT_EXCEEDS_CASH = "SHORT_EXCEEDS_CASH"

TRIGGER_PRECEDENCE: tuple[Trigger, ...] = (
    Trigger.MALFORMED_DECISION, Trigger.ILLEGAL_RATING,
    Trigger.POSITION_LIMIT, Trigger.SHORT_EXCEEDS_CASH,
)

@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class GuardrailLimits:
    max_position_pct: float = 0.10
    max_short_pct_of_cash: float = 1.0
    def as_dict(self) -> dict[str, float]          # stable key order

@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Decision:
    rating: str
    size_pct: float
    short_amount: float
    available_cash: float
    instrument_id: str | None = None               # no clock field, by design

@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class AuditRecord:
    record_id: str
    trigger: Trigger
    observed_value: object
    configured_limit: object
    action: str = AUDIT_ACTION_REVIEW_HOLD
    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, object]         # stable key order

@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class GuardrailResult:
    decision: Decision
    passed: bool
    audit: AuditRecord | None

class GuardrailError(ValueError): ...              # invalid limits / constructible-domain violation only

def evaluate_decision(decision: Decision,
                      limits: GuardrailLimits = GuardrailLimits()) -> GuardrailResult
```

**Exception type.** `evaluate_decision` **never raises for bad decisions** — malformed input is fail-closed into `GuardrailResult(passed=False, trigger=MALFORMED_DECISION)`. It raises `GuardrailError` only for a *bad limits object* (e.g. `max_position_pct` negative or `NaN`): a configuration fault is not a decision, and silently "rejecting" on a broken config would hide it.

**Semantics (pinned, inlined as comments in the module docstring):**
- `size_pct`: reject iff `size_pct > max_position_pct`. **`0.10` accepted; `0.1000001` rejected.**
- Short: reject iff `short_amount > available_cash * max_short_pct_of_cash`, i.e. with `1.0` **`short == cash` accepted**, `short > cash` rejected. The constant's arithmetic reading is documented (pinned R4).
- Zero cash: `short == cash == 0` is **accepted** (literal pin, pinned R8), asserted explicitly and commented as an intentional pin.
- Rating: exact, case-sensitive membership in `VALID_RATINGS`; no strip/casefold/aliases.
- **Malformed** (fail-closed → `MALFORMED_DECISION`): `rating` not a `str` (`None`, `0`, `b"Buy"`, list); any of `size_pct`/`short_amount`/`available_cash` not `int`/`float` (excluding `bool`) or not finite (`NaN`, `±inf`, `Decimal`); `size_pct < 0`; `short_amount < 0`; `available_cash < 0`; `decision` not a `Decision`.
- Multi-violation: exactly **one** record, named by the highest-precedence trigger in `TRIGGER_PRECEDENCE`.
- Contract invariants (asserted): `passed is True ⟺ audit is None ⟺ decision is the input object`; `passed is False ⟹ audit is not None and result.decision.rating == "Hold"` and the returned decision `is not` the input.

**ID derivation.**
```
record_id = "gr-" + sha256(json.dumps({
    "trigger":    trigger.value,
    "observed":   _canon(observed_value),
    "limit":      _canon(configured_limit),
    "action":     action,
}, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=True)).hexdigest()[:16]
_canon(x) = float.hex(x) if isinstance(x, float) else x        # NaN/inf stay injective
```
Deterministic, no clock, no UUID, no counter. For error-path `observed_value` the record uses a short reason code (`"not-a-decision"`, `"rating-not-a-string"`, `"size_pct-nan"`, …) so the hash input is always canonicalisable.

**Collaboration handling (the one call I make, stated as a decision you can overturn):**
- `AuditRecord` is `frozen` and not hashable-by-content, so "collision" means *the same `record_id` for different content*.
- **Construction** path: a content hash is a function of content, so identical input inevitably yields an identical `record_id`. I therefore rule that **`record_id` collision is only detectable at an aggregation boundary**. Implementing a rejecting constructor would break determinism (G6), which is a higher-priority pin.
- So `AuditRecord.from_...`-style construction is *not* given collision rejection; instead the module exposes the guard that implements the pin:

```python
class AuditLog:
    def add(self, record: AuditRecord) -> None    # raises GuardrailError on record_id collision
    def records(self) -> tuple[AuditRecord, ...]
```
This raises `GuardrailError("record_id collision: <id>")` and **never overwrites** (pinned requirement). The acceptance test builds two *distinct* records that are forced to the same `record_id` (by constructing a record with a hand-specified id — the only way to simulate a hash collision) and asserts rejection + that the first record survives. **Is this acceptable, or do you want collision rejection to live somewhere else (or be dropped)?** — flagged for your approval, see §6, risk 6.

**Module purity.** Imports restricted to `dataclasses`, `enum`, `typing`, `json`, `hashlib`, `math`. No clock, network, LLM.

##### 2.2 `src/trace_recorder.py` — ADR-003 / REQ-TRACEABILITY / INV-TRACE-COMPLETENESS

```python
class TraceError(ValueError): ...                  # invalid snapshot / timestamp / duplicate

@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class DataSnapshot:
    snapshot_id: str
    data_source: str
    fetch_timestamp: str                           # caller-supplied UTC ISO-8601

@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class TraceLink:
    link_id: str
    assertion_id: str
    referenced_data_snapshot_id: str
    critical: bool                                 # explicit flag only

@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class AuditFinding:
    assertion_id: str
    reason: str                                    # MISSING_LINK | DANGLING_SNAPSHOT | MULTI_LINK |
                                                   # DUPLICATE_LINK | UNKNOWN_FINAL_REFERENCE | NO_FINAL_DECISION | NO_EVIDENCE
    referenced_data_snapshot_id: str | None

@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class AuditReport:
    traceable: bool
    checked_links: int
    resolved_links: int
    findings: tuple[AuditFinding, ...]             # empty iff traceable
    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, object]         # stable key order

class TraceRecorder:
    def __init__(self) -> None
    def record_snapshot(self, *, snapshot_id: str, data_source: str,
                        fetch_timestamp: str) -> DataSnapshot
    def record_assertion(self, *, assertion_id: str, referenced_data_snapshot_id: str,
                         critical: bool) -> TraceLink
    def record_final_decision(self, *, decision_id: str,
                              referenced_snapshot_ids: Sequence[str]) -> None
    def audit(self) -> AuditReport
    def render_table(self) -> list[dict[str, str]]
```

**Consistency fixes over the architecture sketch** (argument-driven; both are strict strengthening, no pin changed):
- **`critical` is keyword-only with no default.** The sketch had `critical: bool` after a keyword-only marker, which silently forces the caller to write it — but a positional-looking `bool` is exactly the near-miss that lets `critical` be dropped. No default ⇒ `TypeError` on omission ⇒ the "explicit flag" pin is enforced by the signature, not by discipline.
- **`TraceLink` gains `snapshot_id`**? **No.** It keeps only `referenced_data_snapshot_id`; `data_source`/`fetch_timestamp` live on the snapshot and are joined at `audit()`/`render_table()` time, exactly as the pinned chain (`requirements.yaml:113-114`) is shaped.

**Behaviour:**
- `record_snapshot` validates non-empty `snapshot_id`/`data_source`; `fetch_timestamp` must round-trip `datetime.fromisoformat`, be tz-aware, and have a **zero UTC offset** (`+00:00`/`Z`). Raises `TraceError` otherwise. Duplicate `snapshot_id` → `TraceError` (never overwrite).
- `record_assertion` **never drops**: a link to an unknown snapshot is stored and surfaced as `DANGLING_SNAPSHOT`. Duplicate `link_id` → `TraceError`.
- `record_final_decision` stores `decision_id` + refs; calling it twice → `TraceError` (a decision is final once).
- `audit()` computes `N` = assertions **flagged** critical (flags are the ground truth, not surviving links) and `M` = critical links that resolve to a recorded snapshot; `traceable` requires `M == N` **and** ≥1 final-decision reference **and** every finding-free walk of the final decision's links. A missing link, a dangling link, or a zero-reference decision is a failure, never a warning.
- `render_table()` is a **pure function of the recorder's contents** (the architecture sketch drew it only from links; I render every snapshot **and** every link, one row per link, joined with its snapshot, with columnar keys `assertion_id, link_id, critical, referenced_data_snapshot_id, data_source, fetch_timestamp`). Row order = insertion order. Callable at any time; one row per recorded link.
- No module-level mutable state.

**ID derivation.**
```
link_id = "tl-" + sha256(f"{assertion_id}\x1f{referenced_data_snapshot_id}".encode()).hexdigest()[:16]
```
Re-asserting the same (assertion, snapshot) pair therefore **collides by construction** → `TraceError`, which is the duplicate-record obligation. Note the consequence I am accepting and stating: **an assertion may cite only one snapshot**; multi-evidence assertions must be recorded as distinct assertion ids. That is a real semantic narrowing versus "every critical assertion is linked to ≥1 snapshot". **Flagged for approval** (§6, risk 7).

**Clock ban.** Imports restricted to `dataclasses`, `enum`, `typing`, `hashlib`, `datetime` (parsing only). `datetime.now`/`.today`/`time.time`/`uuid4` are **AST-banned**, not merely unused.

##### 4.3 Negative-test design (`G9`, `T9`) — how they avoid testing the mock

Both negatives are built so the **assertion under test** is the *same expression* used by the positive test, factored into a module-level helper:

- `test_guardrail.py` has `def zero_escapes(guardrail_fn, cases) -> int` used by **both** G3 (real) and G9 (patched). G9 asserts `zero_escapes(patched, cases) != 0` (i.e. the gate *would* fail), while asserting `zero_escapes(real, cases) == 0`. If the helper were vacuous (`cases == []`), G3 would fail; if the real function always passed, G3 would fail; if the patch did not defeat the check, G9 would fail. Three distinct failure modes.
- `test_traceability.py` has `def completeness_gap(recorder, fixtures) -> int` used by T3 and T9 identically. T9's recorder subclasses `TraceRecorder` and drops the **second** critical link via `super().record_assertion` skipping — the real code path is still exercised for the other links, so the test measures the recorder's gate, not a hand-written fake that bypasses it.

| 6 | **Collision rejection has no natural call site** — a content hash of identical content can never differ, so a rejecting *constructor* would break determinism (G6). | Implemented on `AuditLog.add` / `TraceRecorder.record_assertion` where aggregation exists; **flagged in §2.1 for your decision**.
